givens.sourceText: thermodynamic relation between Gibbs energy and reaction quotient
electrochemical relation between Gibbs energy and cell potential

qualitativeClaims.claim: Combine ΔG = ΔG° + RT ln Q with ΔG = -nFE_cell and ΔG° = -nFE°_cell to get -nFE_cell = -nFE°_cell + RT ln Q, then divide by -nF.
At 298 K with R = 8.314 J/(mol·K), F = 96485 C/mol, and ln Q = 2.303 log Q, the equation becomes the common base-10 form.
qualitativeClaims.expected: E_cell = E°_cell - (0.0592/n) log Q at 298 K

qualitativeClaims.claim: As Q increases, ln Q (and log Q) increases, so the subtracted term (RT/nF) ln Q grows and E_cell decreases monotonically; dE/dQ = -RT/(nFQ) < 0.
When Q = 1, ln Q = 0 and E_cell = E°_cell; when Q > 1 (products favoured), E_cell < E°_cell; when Q < 1, E_cell > E°_cell.
qualitativeClaims.expected: E_cell = E°_cell at Q = 1; E_cell < E°_cell for Q > 1; E_cell > E°_cell for Q < 1

qualitativeClaims.claim: At equilibrium Q = K and ΔG = 0, so E_cell = 0, giving E°_cell = (RT/nF) ln K; a dead battery corresponds to Q = K.
qualitativeClaims.expected: E_cell = 0 when Q = K; E°_cell = (RT/nF) ln K

lawIds: van't Hoff reaction isotherm: ΔG = ΔG° + RT ln Q
Nernst equation: E = E° - (RT/nF) ln Q
assumptions: Ideal behaviour: activities approximated by concentrations/pressures in Q
Constant temperature, typically 298 K for the 0.0592 V form
n is the moles of electrons transferred in the balanced half-reactions
E°_cell is the standard potential with all species at unit activity
A verified illustration is required by the question's spatial or explicit visual request.
